title: Global Status And Error Surface

oracle.positive: Invalid command/OCCT diagnostic visible in status, not lost in console
oracle.negative: Error popup cannot swallow escape/cancel state or dismiss silently

reviewer.role: project owner (human reviewer) running the app on Windows

checks_run: RED: cargo test -p om9-app --test global_status_surface -> 9 passed; 1 failed. The one product defect: an unknown command was reported as 'unsupported unknown/unavailable command' without naming what the user typed.
GREEN: cargo test -p om9-app --test global_status_surface -> 10 passed; 0 failed (G1..G10 visible/retrievable, X1..X6 no swallowed state)
cargo test --workspace -j 2: every group ok; cargo check --workspace --all-targets: exit 0
cargo fmt --check: exit 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0

real window: om9.exe --ui-audit writes a receipt carrying status_kind, status_message and status_tail (OM9-L4-01-01-007-04.integration.log); L3-002 size matrix 14/14 PASS; L3-003 panel scenarios 7/7 PASS
code_change: ui.rs::submit_draft: an unknown command is now reported as 'unknown command: <what was typed>' in both the status line and the command history, instead of the generic refusal that did not name it.
ui/chrome.rs::status_bar_ui: hovering the status line lists the recent messages (the bounded tail), so a diagnostic the user did not read when it appeared is still reachable.
ui.rs::dock_receipt: the receipt carries status_kind, status_message and status_tail, so an evaluator can check the surface after the fact.

manual_reviewer_checklist.scope_note: The lifetime and the Esc behaviour are machine-proven; how the line and its hover read on screen is the owner's call.

items.step: Type a command the program does not have (for example NotACommand) and press Enter.
items.machine_proven: G1: the line reads 'Error: unknown command: NotACommand', the same text is in the history, and the tail carries it.
items.human_must_verify: The red-ish error line names the command you typed, and you can find the same line by scrolling the command history.

items.step: After that failure, run a command that works (for example Line).
items.machine_proven: G2: the failure stays; complete_success refuses while a failure is unacknowledged.
items.human_must_verify: The error line is still there after the successful command, and Dismiss is the only thing that clears it.

items.step: Hover the status line after a few messages have gone by.
items.machine_proven: G9/G10: the tail keeps the last eight messages, oldest first, and a second failure keeps the first.
items.human_must_verify: The hover lists the recent messages, so a warning you missed is still readable.

items.step: With a failure on the line, start a command (for example Line) and press Escape.
items.machine_proven: X1/X2: Escape still cancels the command and does not dismiss the failure.
items.human_must_verify: Escape cancels the command, the failure stays, and no dialog appears that traps the keyboard.

items.step: Repeat the invalid command with a very long line, and with a warning-producing action (for example a floating menu that has to be pulled back inside).
items.machine_proven: G5/G7: a warning is visible without becoming a failure; a long diagnostic is cut at 512 bytes on a character boundary.
items.human_must_verify: Nothing overflows the status bar, the text stays readable and the summary on the right is still elided sensibly.
